answer.rationale: Hard 18% spend cut plus a 14-day hard expiry rules out a pure status-quo renew, but the line is at 94% with no buffer, so a primary cutover would raise delivery risk and violate the TCO-without-added-risk objective. Incumbent already refused a mid-cycle reopen, yet renewal is the leverage point: c4 says benchmarking (now a mandate-meeting low-cost quote) moved price and terms at renewal, and c6 says a longer commitment unlocked volume pricing without shrinking scope—together that is the only path that can hit cost while keeping incumbent integration (c1). c2 makes the quote a credible BATNA but last year’s quick onboarding is unverified at current utilization, so it is not yet a switch decision. Not deferring (no auto-renew; this is not the non-critical c5 case) and not adding a second source as the single action (does not replace the expiring primary). Verifying c4 and c2 before committing; outcome of a 14-day negotiate remains uncertain.
